title: OSHA crane signal person qualifications practice questions
description: Practice questions on who must qualify crane signal persons, the two options, documentation, re-assessment and the requirements (29 CFR 1926.1428).

questions.topic: Who must make sure, and when
questions.question: No third party qualified evaluator has documented a worker's qualifications, and no qualified evaluator of the employer has assessed the worker. The superintendent wants the worker to signal a crane anyway because the worker has signaled cranes for ten years. How does 1926.1428(a) treat that?

options.A: It complies, because ten years of signaling experience stands in for an assessment
options.B: It falls short, because the requirement must be met by using either Option (1) or Option (2)
options.C: It complies, if the crane operator signs off on the worker's signals
options.D: It complies, if the worker holds a crane operator certification

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure that each signal person meets the Qualification Requirements "prior to giving any signals", and "This requirement must be met by using either Option (1) or Option (2) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Who must make sure, and when
questions.question: A contractor assigns a newly hired laborer to signal a crane on the first morning and plans to have the laborer assessed at the end of the week. How does 1926.1428(a) treat that plan?

options.A: It complies, because the assessment comes within the first 30 days
options.B: It complies, if the crane operator agrees to accept the laborer's signals in the meantime
options.C: It falls short, because the employer must ensure the signal person meets the Qualification Requirements prior to giving any signals
options.D: It complies, if a second signal person stands next to the laborer

questions.explanation: "The employer of the signal person must ensure that each signal person meets the Qualification Requirements (paragraph (c) of this section) prior to giving any signals."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An independent entity that, due to its independence and expertise, has demonstrated that it is competent in accurately assessing signal persons gives a worker documentation from its assessment. If the worker's employer relies on that documentation, which route in 1926.1428(a) is it using?

options.D: None; documentation from outside the employer cannot be used

questions.explanation: Option (1) is headed "Third party qualified evaluator": "The signal person has documentation from a third party qualified evaluator" showing that the signal person meets the Qualification Requirements.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under Option (1) in 1926.1428(a)(1), what must the third party qualified evaluator's documentation show?

options.A: The number of hours the signal person has worked near cranes
options.B: That the signal person also holds crane operator certification
options.C: The rated capacity of each crane the signal person will direct
options.D: That the signal person meets the Qualification Requirements

questions.explanation: Under Option (1), "The signal person has documentation from a third party qualified evaluator ... showing that the signal person meets the Qualification Requirements (see paragraph (c) of this section)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under Option (2) in 1926.1428(a)(2), what must the employer's qualified evaluator provide once it determines that the individual meets the Qualification Requirements?

options.A: A wallet card issued by OSHA
options.C: A report to the crane's manufacturer
options.D: A copy of the crane operator's certification

questions.explanation: The employer's qualified evaluator "assesses the individual and determines that the individual meets the Qualification Requirements (see paragraph (c) of this section) and provides documentation of that determination."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A signal person was assessed and documented by Employer X's own qualified evaluator under Option (2). She then goes to work for Employer Y, which wants her to signal on its crane next week. What must happen before she gives signals for Employer Y?

options.A: Nothing; Employer Y may rely on Employer X's documentation if it is kept at the site
options.B: Nothing for the first year; Employer Y may rely on Employer X's assessment until then
options.C: Employer Y must have the requirement met through Option (1) or Option (2), because Employer X's assessment is not portable
options.D: Nothing, if the crane operator agrees to accept her signals

questions.explanation: "An assessment by an employer's qualified evaluator under this option is not portable—other employers are not permitted to use it to meet the requirements of this section." The requirement "must be met by using either Option (1) or Option (2) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For what period does 1926.1428(a)(3) require the employer to make the signal person's qualification documentation available at the site?

options.A: While the signal person is employed by the employer
options.B: For three years after the signal person's last lift
options.C: Only until the crane's next annual inspection
options.D: Only on the first day the signal person works at the site

questions.explanation: "The employer must make the documentation for whichever option is used available at the site while the signal person is employed by the employer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A signal person's documentation lists hand signals only. Her employer now wants her to direct a lift by radio. Under 1926.1428, what is needed before she signals by radio?

options.A: Nothing; documentation for one type of signaling covers every type
options.B: Only the crane operator's agreement to accept her radio signals
options.C: Only a second signal person giving hand signals at the same time
options.D: A showing, under Option (1) or Option (2), that she meets the Qualification Requirements for radio signals, with documentation that specifies radio signaling

questions.explanation: "The documentation must specify each type of signaling (e.g. hand signals, radio signals, etc.) for which the signal person meets the requirements of paragraph (c) of this section." Each signal person must "Know and understand the type of signals used" and "Be competent in the application of the type of signals used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An employer relies on a signal person's documentation from a third party qualified evaluator. The employer says the site-availability duty in 1926.1428(a)(3) covers only assessments made by its own qualified evaluator. Is the employer right?

options.A: Yes; in that case only the third party qualified evaluator keeps the documentation
options.B: No; the employer must make the documentation for whichever option is used available at the site
options.C: Yes; in that case the documentation needs to be kept only at the employer's main office
options.D: Yes; in that case only the signal person keeps the documentation

questions.explanation: "The employer must make the documentation for whichever option is used available at the site while the signal person is employed by the employer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: When a signal person falls short
questions.question: Under 1926.1428(b), what triggers the employer's duty to stop an individual from continuing to work as a signal person?

options.A: Subsequent actions by the signal person indicate that the individual does not meet the Qualification Requirements
options.B: The signal person has not given signals for 30 days
options.C: The crane is moved to a new site
options.D: A new operator starts work on the crane

questions.explanation: Paragraph (b) applies "If subsequent actions by the signal person indicate that the individual does not meet the Qualification Requirements".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: When a signal person falls short
questions.question: A signal person's actions on the job showed that he does not meet the Qualification Requirements, so his employer took him off signaling. He has now finished re-training, but no re-assessment has been made yet. Under 1926.1428(b), may he go back to work as a signal person?

options.A: Yes, because re-training has been provided
options.B: Yes, if the operator watches his signals closely
options.C: No; first a re-assessment made in accordance with paragraph (a) must confirm that he meets the Qualification Requirements
options.D: Yes, but for hand signals only

questions.explanation: The employer must not allow the individual to continue working as a signal person "until re-training is provided and a re-assessment is made in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section that confirms that the individual meets the Qualification Requirements."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An evaluator is preparing the equipment part of a signal person assessment. Under 1926.1428(c)(3), what understanding of equipment operation and limitations must the signal person have?

options.A: Only the crane's maximum boom length
options.B: None; equipment operation is a matter for the operator alone
options.C: Only the rated capacity of each crane on the site
options.D: A basic understanding, including the crane dynamics involved in swinging and stopping loads and boom deflection from hoisting loads

questions.explanation: Each signal person must "Have a basic understanding of equipment operation and limitations, including the crane dynamics involved in swinging and stopping loads and boom deflection from hoisting loads."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: In an oral test, a worker correctly explains the signals used on the job, the equipment's operation and limitations, and the relevant signal rules. In the practical test, the worker gives contradictory directions and loses track of the load. Which Qualification Requirement in 1926.1428(c) has the worker not shown?

options.A: Being competent in the application of the type of signals used
options.B: Knowing and understanding the type of signals used
options.C: Having a basic understanding of equipment operation and limitations
options.D: Knowing and understanding the relevant requirements of §§ 1926.1419 through 1926.1422 and 1926.1428

questions.explanation: Each signal person must "Be competent in the application of the type of signals used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An evaluator has confirmed that a worker knows and understands the signals used, is competent in applying them and has a basic understanding of equipment operation and limitations, but has not checked the worker on any regulatory requirements. Which Qualification Requirement in 1926.1428(c) is still left to show?

options.B: Knowing and understanding the relevant requirements of §§ 1926.1419 through 1926.1422 and 1926.1428
options.C: Having signaled under supervision for a set number of hours
options.D: Being able to inspect the crane's rigging

questions.explanation: Each signal person must "Know and understand the relevant requirements of §§ 1926.1419 through 1926.1422 and 1926.1428."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A worker passes a written test covering everything in 1926.1428(c)(1) through (4), but the evaluator never has the worker give signals in a practical test. Has the worker met (c)(5)?

options.A: Yes, because a written test alone is enough
options.B: Yes, if the worker has signaled on other jobs before
options.C: Yes, if the crane operator vouches for the worker
options.D: No; (c)(5) requires the demonstration through an oral or written test, and through a practical test

questions.explanation: Each signal person must "Demonstrate that he/she meets the requirements in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) of this section through an oral or written test, and through a practical test."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1428(c)(5), what must a signal person demonstrate through testing?

options.A: That the signal person meets the operator requirements of § 1926.1427
options.B: Only that he/she can give signals during a lift
options.C: That he/she meets the requirements in (c)(1) through (4): the signals used, their application, equipment operation and limitations, and the relevant rules
options.D: That the crane's rated capacity is not exceeded

questions.explanation: Each signal person must "Demonstrate that he/she meets the requirements in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) of this section through an oral or written test, and through a practical test."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1428, Signal person qualifications (as of Nov 4, 2026)
